## Purpose

This SOP describes the end-to-end laboratory workflow for environmental
DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, from receipt of field-collected water filter
samples through DNA extraction, PCR amplification, library preparation,
sequencing, and bioinformatics analysis. eDNA metabarcoding combines
universal or group-specific primers with high-throughput sequencing to
detect and characterize aquatic biodiversity from water samples without
capturing organisms [@taberlet2012; @deiner2017].

This SOP serves as the integrating document that ties together the
field collection procedures in
[SOP-F700](../field_sops/SOP-F700-edna-field-sampling.qmd) with the
molecular and computational SOPs in the L700 series. It does not
repeat detailed procedures described in other SOPs but provides the
eDNA-specific modifications, QC requirements, and decision points that
distinguish eDNA metabarcoding from standard amplicon sequencing of
soil or tissue samples.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Laboratory processing of eDNA water samples for
  multi-species detection via amplicon sequencing on Illumina
  platforms; target taxa include fish (12S), amphibians (16S/12S),
  macroinvertebrates (COI), and general biodiversity surveys
  (18S, COI)
- **Does not apply to:** Species-specific eDNA detection by qPCR or
  ddPCR (single-species assays); soil microbial community analysis
  (see [SOP-L704](SOP-L704-amplicon-library-prep.qmd) and
  [SOP-L705](SOP-L705-bioinformatics-pipeline.qmd)); field collection
  procedures (see
  [SOP-F700](../field_sops/SOP-F700-edna-field-sampling.qmd))
- **Location:** Molecular biology bench, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve target markers, primers, and sequencing plan |
| Trained Personnel | Process samples per this SOP; maintain contamination controls |
| New Students      | Complete eDNA-specific contamination training before participating |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Lysis buffers (guanidine salts), ethanol, SPRI beads,
  and DNA stains. See individual SOP safety sections for details.
- **Biological:** eDNA samples may originate from water bodies
  containing pathogens. Handle with standard precautions.
- **UV radiation:** If using UV transilluminator for gel imaging.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (changed frequently; mandatory at all steps)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## Workflow Overview

The eDNA metabarcoding workflow consists of six stages. Each stage
references a detailed SOP.

| Stage | Description                          | SOP Reference |
|:------|:-------------------------------------|:--------------|
| 1     | Field collection and preservation    | [F700](../field_sops/SOP-F700-edna-field-sampling.qmd) |
| 2     | DNA extraction from filters          | [L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) |
| 3     | PCR amplification and verification   | [L703](SOP-L703-pcr-gel-electrophoresis.qmd) |
| 4     | Library preparation and sequencing   | [L704](SOP-L704-amplicon-library-prep.qmd) |
| 5     | Bioinformatics (QIIME 2 / DADA2)    | [L705](SOP-L705-bioinformatics-pipeline.qmd) |
| 6     | Taxonomic interpretation and reporting | This SOP, Section 6.6 |


## Procedure: eDNA-Specific Modifications

### Sample Receipt and Logging

1. Upon receipt from the field, verify that all samples match the chain
   of custody form per
   [SOP-F008](../field_sops/SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd).
2. Inspect Sterivex capsules or filter bags for integrity (no leaks,
   caps intact, preservative present).
3. Log each sample in the lab notebook and
   [Freezer Inventory Google Sheet](<!-- LINK_PLACEHOLDER -->).
4. Store preserved filters at -20 C (short-term) or -80 C (long-term)
   until extraction.

### DNA Extraction from Filters

Follow [SOP-L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) with the following
eDNA-specific modifications:

- **Sterivex capsules:** Open the capsule aseptically using a sterile
  razor blade or the Sterivex extraction adapter. Transfer the membrane
  into the PowerBead Pro tube using sterile forceps. If Longmire's buffer
  was used as preservative, add the buffer to the bead tube as well.
- **Open membrane filters:** Transfer the folded filter directly into
  the bead tube using sterile forceps.
- **Extraction blanks:** Process one extraction blank per batch. For
  eDNA, this means running an empty bead tube through the full protocol.
- **Field blanks:** The field blank filter (from
  [SOP-F700](../field_sops/SOP-F700-edna-field-sampling.qmd)) is
  extracted alongside samples and serves as the primary contamination
  control for the entire field-to-lab chain.

### Inhibition Testing

eDNA extracts from natural waters frequently contain PCR inhibitors
(humic acids, tannins, metal ions) [@mckee2015]. Test for inhibition
before committing to full library preparation:

1. Run an internal positive control (IPC) qPCR assay on a subset of
   extracts (or all extracts, if the batch is small). The IPC uses a
   synthetic DNA target spiked into the PCR reaction at a known
   concentration.
2. If the IPC C~t~ value shifts by more than 2 cycles compared to the
   uninhibited control, the extract is inhibited.
3. For inhibited samples, dilute the extract 1:5 or 1:10 with
   nuclease-free water and retest. Alternatively, clean the extract
   using a OneStep PCR Inhibitor Removal Kit (Zymo Research).

### Primer Selection for eDNA Metabarcoding

| Target Taxa          | Marker   | Primers              | Amplicon | Reference         |
|:---------------------|:---------|:---------------------|:---------|:------------------|
| Fish                 | 12S rRNA | MiFish-U-F / MiFish-U-R | ~170 bp | @miya2015         |
| Amphibians           | 16S rRNA | 16Smam / 16Smam-R (modified) | ~250 bp | @vences2005  |
| Macroinvertebrates   | COI      | mlCOIintF / jgHCO2198 | ~313 bp | @leray2013        |
| General eukaryotes   | 18S rRNA | Euk1391f / EukBr     | ~130 bp  | @amaralzettler2009 |
| General eukaryotes   | COI      | fwhF2 / fwhR2n       | ~205 bp  | @vamos2022         |

::: {.callout-note}
Primer choice determines which taxa can be detected. Discuss target taxa
and primer selection with the PI before beginning library preparation.
Multi-marker approaches (e.g., 12S + COI) provide broader taxonomic
coverage but require separate library preparations and sequencing runs
[@deiner2017].
:::

### PCR and Library Preparation

Follow [SOP-L703](SOP-L703-pcr-gel-electrophoresis.qmd) for initial PCR
screening and [SOP-L704](SOP-L704-amplicon-library-prep.qmd) for library
preparation, with these eDNA-specific considerations:

- **Replicates:** Run 3 independent PCR replicates per sample to improve
  detection probability for rare species [@ficetola2015]. Pool the
  replicates after PCR1 before cleanup and indexing.
- **Cycle number:** Use 35 cycles for PCR1 (higher than standard 16S
  amplicon work) because eDNA concentrations are typically very low.
  Be aware that additional cycles increase the risk of chimera formation
  and tag-jumping [@schnell2015].
- **Blocking primers (optional):** If non-target taxa (e.g., human DNA)
  dominate the PCR product, consider using blocking primers or PNA
  (peptide nucleic acid) clamps to suppress amplification of non-target
  sequences.
- **Controls:** In addition to the standard NTC and extraction blank,
  include the field blank and (if available) a positive control
  consisting of a mock community of known species at known
  concentrations.

### Bioinformatics and Taxonomic Assignment

Follow [SOP-L705](SOP-L705-bioinformatics-pipeline.qmd) for denoising
and taxonomic classification, with these modifications:

- **Reference database:** Use a curated database matched to the marker
  and target taxa:
  - 12S fish: MitoFish or MIDORI2
  - COI: BOLD / MIDORI2
  - 16S/18S: SILVA or GenBank nt
- **Species-level assignment:** For eDNA, species-level identification
  is the primary goal (unlike microbiome studies where genus-level is
  often sufficient). Use BLAST-based classification (`classify-consensus-
  blast` in QIIME 2) in addition to or instead of the Naive Bayes
  classifier for improved species-level resolution [@goldberg2016].
- **Decontamination:** Use the `decontam` R package to identify and
  remove contaminant ASVs using the field blank and extraction blank
  data [@davis2018].
- **Detection criteria:** An ASV is considered a positive detection for
  a species only if:
  1. It matches a reference sequence at greater than or equal to 97--99%
     identity (marker-dependent)
  2. It is absent from all negative controls (field blank, extraction
     blank, NTC), or its abundance in the sample exceeds 10x the
     abundance in the highest-read control
  3. It is detected in at least 2 of 3 PCR replicates (if replicates
     were sequenced independently) [@ficetola2015]

### Reporting

eDNA metabarcoding results are reported as a species detection list per
site with the following metadata:

- ASV sequence and percent identity to reference
- Number of reads per ASV per sample
- Detection across replicates (e.g., detected in 2/3 replicates)
- Negative control results
- Any taxa flagged as potential contaminants

::: {.callout-important}
eDNA metabarcoding provides presence/detection data. Quantitative
interpretation of read counts as species abundance is not recommended
without careful validation, because PCR amplification bias, primer
affinity, and DNA shedding rates vary among taxa [@kelly2019].
:::


## Quality Control

- **Field blanks:** Must be negative for all target taxa. Any target
  taxon detected in a field blank compromises the detection claim for
  that taxon across all samples in the same sampling event.
- **Extraction blanks:** Must be negative. Positive extraction blanks
  indicate lab contamination; the entire extraction batch is suspect.
- **NTC:** Must be negative. Positive NTCs indicate PCR contamination.
- **Positive control (mock community):** Must recover all expected
  species. Failure to detect a known species in the mock community
  indicates primer bias or PCR failure.
- **Replication:** A minimum of 3 PCR replicates per sample is
  recommended for occupancy-based detection analyses.
- Document all control results in the project data file and report
  alongside species detections.

## Training Record

Before processing eDNA samples independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and all related SOPs (F700, L700, L703, L704, L705)
2. Demonstrate aseptic filter handling and extraction under supervision
3. Complete an eDNA-specific contamination awareness session covering
   pre-PCR/post-PCR separation, filter handling, and control
   interpretation
4. Process a supervised batch including field blank, extraction blank,
   and positive control with clean results
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
